Point moved from La Haye-du-Puits (v1, about 11 km south) to the ground south of Pont l'Abbé: Les Moitiers-en-Bauptois centre is about 2 km south-southwest of the Pont l'Abbé hamlet (OSM), within the 1.5-mile depth. location_represents is now objective (the planned bridgehead), not front_line_point. Documented elsewhere on 17 June: the 82d secured the causeway over the Prairies Marécageuses south of St. Sauveur-le-Vicomte by that night (Utah Beach to Cherbourg, ch. 8); that is about 7.5 km west and is not this row's point. location_name: Drop zones around Groesbeek (DZ N south of Groesbeek), Gelderland, Netherlands
composing_units: attached: British 2nd Irish Guards (Guards Armoured Division) from 16 September
current_activity: parachute and glider landing on drop zones around Groesbeek (Market Garden)
notes: Event date: 17 September 1944; the 82nd's parachute lift dropped 12:50–14:00, the division headquarters party jumped about 13:06 and the gliders landed about 13:50 on DZ N south of Groesbeek (TracesOfWar; 82nd Airborne Division, Operation Market historical data). Event definition: the airborne landing. The division command post (CHAMPION, about 1,000 yards west of Groesbeek, set up about 17:00) is a separate row (hq_move). Location: the point is the Groesbeek landing area (OpenStreetMap Nominatim, Groesbeek centroid), not the CMH command-post vicinity of Nijmegen that this row used before. Relationship: for Market Garden British I Airborne Corps held operational control of the 82nd and 101st Airborne Divisions; the CMH table shows the division as under I Airborne Corps from 17 September. XVIII Airborne Corps (assigned from 12 August, ended 17 September per Wikipedia) stayed in England. First Allied Airborne Army was the higher Allied command over both corps.

current_activity: arrives at Werbomont after being diverted from Bastogne
notes: Event date: 18 December 1944 (Ardennes p342: on the morning of 18 December the 82d Airborne Division started for Bastogne but was diverted short of its destination and ordered to Werbomont; part of the division arrived in the village at dark and opened the division command post; the bulk moved into the area during the night). Event definition: the division reaches the northern shoulder from Sissonne and Camp Mourmelon and forms the left of the First Army front; the command post opens at Werbomont at nightfall. Relationship: First Allied Airborne Army assigned (CMH table); the XVIII Airborne Corps becomes operational the next day and attaches the division (see the next row). Location: Werbomont village; the atlas also lists Werbomont on 18 December. Coordinates: Wikipedia (fr): Werbomont. Event support: high (Green Book narrative and atlas agree).
